merge_corrections.what: NO CORRECTION NEEDED. Zero errors and zero warnings. The rework replaced the seven repeated control texts with sixty-four unique ones, one per process, and narrowed the repeated OSHA citation to the subsection that constrains each process rather than the section as a whole. Both were the rejection grounds and both are fixed.
accepted_from_submitter: Sixty-four controls, every one unique across thirty-two processes - from a file that previously carried seven texts for the whole category.

29 CFR 1910.269 cited at the subsection that bites rather than at the section: (c) job briefing where the process is a briefing, (l) minimum approach distance where it is proximity, (a)(3) host and contract employer information transfer where a contractor is on site.
18.4.4 named as the issuer of a clearance rather than 4.0 claiming to issue one - the cross-category boundary held without being restated in the brief.
MUTCD cited for work-zone traffic control, which is the correct authority and is public law.
merge_corrections.models_built_here: Twelve artifacts, 6 BPMN, 3 DMN and 3 CMMN. The specification names them; only this side has the generator.
merge_corrections.open_finding_notation_why: OPEN FINDING, ADDED AFTER THE MERGE NOTE ABOVE WAS WRITTEN. That note said no correction was needed, and on the two rejection grounds it was right. Building the behaviour models surfaced a third instance of the same defect family: notation.why - the rationale for why a process is drawn in a given notation - is one text on 24 of the 32 processes. It states the notation RULE ('the process has a repeatable start, ordered activities and a defined completion outcome') rather than which repeatable start THIS process has. Nothing in it is false; it is the BPMN test, correctly applied. But fifteen of the seventeen merged categories carry a distinct rationale on every process and none shares one on more than two. Recorded rather than fixed, and now a WARNING in validate_spec.py - the third check of this shape after control reuse and judgment-citation reuse. The pattern across all three is the same: a category-level truth put where a process-level one belongs, in a file that passed every other check because the field was populated.

merge_corrections.what: The open notation.why finding is closed. 32 rationales rewritten, one per process, each naming the repeatable start and the completion outcome for THAT process rather than restating the notation test.
merge_corrections.why: The rationale had been written per notation CLASS, so every BPMN process carried the BPMN test. Nothing asserted was false; what was missing is which start and which outcome, which is the only part a reader cannot derive alone. Material came from each process's own trigger, activities and outputs - no new sources, and nothing else in the submission changed.

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. IEC 61968 defines exchanged work information, OSHA constrains field execution, and EN 17007 provides the process spine. Unsourced field-service detail is labelled judgment.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: Field service management, mobile workforce management and service dispatch are not standards domains. Detailed assignment, dispatch, execution and exception sequences are judgment.
Offline operation, synchronisation conflict resolution, electronic forms, field evidence capture and field-device provisioning are vendor-defined.
No standard specifies complete work-package content. Field review can confirm required local content but cannot claim a universal package definition.
Lone-worker timers and escalation intervals have no permitted cross-commodity standard in the Source Authority Pack.
IEC 61968-3 establishes network-operations interface scope but the pack supplies no detailed method for verifying control-room points after a field change.
Temporary and permanent restoration methods, permit deadlines and jurisdiction acceptance vary by issuing authority; MUTCD governs traffic control, not the restoration permit.

The APQC crosswalk says pcf_id 19225 Monitor work performance in flight has no model group, but 4.1.4 Monitor progress and exception appears to cover that function. The crosswalk and taxonomy need reconciliation.
A clearance is produced by 18.4.4 against a switching plan approved at 18.2.2 under 29 CFR 1910.269(m). Process 4.4.4 validates and consumes it; it does not issue it.

measures.name: Jurisdiction release cycle time
measures.definition: Apply SMRP 5.4.7 from inspection request through jurisdiction acceptance; formula not reproduced.

variants: Accepted on first inspection
Conditional acceptance with minor action
Rejected and returned for corrective restoration

notation.why: Starts at the jurisdiction inspection point and ends in acceptance or corrective work. The utility requests and attends; it does not decide the outcome.

sources.cite: EN 17007:2017 Maintenance process and associated indicators, ACT.7 Finish the tasks, cl. 6.5.8
IEC 61968-6:2015 cl. 4.2 and cl. 5; IEC 61968-11:2013 CIM Work package

SMRP Best Practices 7th Edition, metric 5.4.7
No permitted source defines jurisdiction inspection scheduling, evidence submission or rejection correction.
MUTCD 11th Edition with Revision 1, Part 6 Temporary Traffic Control; local permit conditions remain jurisdiction-specific

regulatory.why: MUTCD governs how this is done, not whether it is done

processes.name: Track restoration against permit deadline
processes.intent: Maintain visibility and escalation for restoration obligations approaching their permitted deadline.
activities: Record the permit or jurisdiction deadline
Compare open restoration with the remaining time
Notify the responsible owner before breach
Escalate an at-risk or overdue obligation
Close tracking on accepted release

trigger.text: An open restoration obligation reaches a monitoring threshold.

inputs.what: Authorised work, scope and current status
Asset, location and prior field record
Assigned resource and operating constraints

outputs.what: Current deadline status and escalation record

controls.text: Compare each open restoration obligation with its permit or jurisdiction deadline and named owner.
Notify before breach and escalate at-risk or overdue work; close tracking only on accepted release.

measures.name: Overdue restoration work
measures.definition: Apply SMRP 5.4.11 to restoration obligations past the permit or jurisdiction due date; formula not reproduced.

variants: On track within the permit window
At risk and escalated before deadline
Overdue with jurisdiction notification required

notation.why: Starts when an open obligation reaches its monitoring threshold and ends with the owner notified or the breach escalated. The deadline is fixed before monitoring begins.
